name: Keep chickens
time: A season to set up, then daily
blurb: Eggs, entertainment and a pest patrol. Chickens are easy to keep alive and hard to keep safe — predators are the real challenge, not the birds.
gear: A coop with a secure run and good ventilation
steps: Check local rules first: many places restrict numbers, or ban cockerels entirely.
Build or buy a coop with proper ventilation but no draughts, and enough space — cramped birds get sick and peck each other.
Predator-proof properly: bury or skirt the wire, use welded mesh rather than chicken wire, and secure it against animals that can open latches.
Start with three or four hens of a docile laying breed, since chickens are miserable alone.
Learn the daily routine: let out, check feed and water, collect eggs, shut in securely at dusk.
Learn the common health issues — red mite, scaly leg, egg binding — and check the birds regularly.
tips: Foxes will dig and reach through wire. Chicken wire keeps chickens in, not predators out.
Egg laying drops in winter and with age. Keeping hens for eggs alone is not economical; keep them because you like them.
proof: A healthy flock that has come through a full year, including winter, with no predator losses.
